title: The Survey
logline: Corporate's anonymous manager survey ranks Michael last in the region, and he hunts down the author of one brutal comment, while Pam works up the nerve to sign up for an art class.
outline: A: Michael is ranked last in an anonymous survey and obsesses over one harsh comment, until he reads the rest. B: Pam wants to take an art class; Roy shrugs, Jim asks to see her sketchbook. C: Dwight investigates the survey with Angela as secretary, discovers she wrote the comment, and protects her. Order: cold, A, B, A, C, A, B, C, A, C, B, tag
theme: What people really think of you
storySoFar: An anonymous manager survey ranked Michael sixth of six (Josh from Stamford was first), with one brutal comment: 'Michael thinks we're a family. We're not. We're people who are stuck in a room together.' Dwight, investigating with Angela as secretary, matched a misspelling ('togethger') to her party memos, realized she wrote it, and protected her by telling Michael the author was unknowable. Michael read the rest of the comments, including 'he's the reason I still work here', and let it go. Pam signed up for a Tuesday art class, 'Drawing from Life', after Roy shrugged and Darryl told her to go; Jim found a sketch of himself asleep in her sketchbook. Earlier: Jan kissed Michael and faxed 'It didn't happen'; corporate will close Stamford or Scranton; Pam kept the invitation Jim picked; Kelly insists she's dating Ryan.

stateChanges.progress: Pam signed up for an art class; Roy shrugged; Jim saw a sketch of himself in her book
Dwight discovered Angela wrote the harsh survey comment and protected her
Michael ranked last in the region's manager survey; Josh from Stamford ranked first

stateChanges.text: Pam's art class: 'Drawing from Life', Tuesdays at Lackawanna Community College
Angela wrote the 'stuck in a room together' comment; only Dwight knows
Dwight's suggestion box, stuffed by Jim

scenes.recap: Dwight opens his new suggestion box and finds forty suggestions, all about himself, all in Jim's handwriting.

beats.caption: opens a shoebox labeled DWIGHT'S SUGGESTION BOX

beats.text: 'Dwight should wear a bell so we know when he's coming.'
'Dwight should only speak in questions on Fridays.' 'Dwight should be in charge of nothing.'
Wow. Lot of feedback. People really engaged with the box.
They're all in your handwriting, Jim.
Or are they in a lot of people's handwriting that looks like mine?

scenes.recap: Michael proudly reads the regional manager survey results aloud and discovers he's last, and one comment hurts.

beats.text: The regional manager survey results are in. Anonymous. Which means honest. Which means great.

beats.caption: flips to the last page, then back, then to the last page

beats.text: Sixth out of six. Josh from Stamford is first. Josh plays squash.
And a comment. 'Michael thinks we're a family. We're not. We're people who are stuck in a room together.'
I didn't write that. I wrote 'Michael is good at birthdays.'

lines: 'Stuck in a room together.' You know who else was stuck in a room together? The Brady Bunch.
And they were a family. Look it up.

scenes.recap: Jim notices an art-class flyer on Pam's desk; she hasn't signed up yet.

beats.text: 'Drawing from Life. Lackawanna Community College. Tuesdays.' Pam Beesly, are you going to art school?
It's one class. And I haven't signed up. It's eighty dollars. It's probably dumb.
It's not dumb. You draw on sticky notes all day. Imagine what you'd do with a whole piece of paper.
I'll ask Roy tonight.

lines: I used to draw every day. In high school I wanted to illustrate children's books.
Then I got a job answering phones. Which I'm also good at. So.

scenes.recap: Michael orders Dwight to find out who wrote the comment; Dwight demands a secretary.

beats.text: Dwight. I need you to find out who wrote it. Quietly. No one can know.
An anonymous survey can be cracked. I'll need typing samples, coffee logs, and a secretary.
Use Angela. She hates everybody equally. She's objective.

lines: Every anonymous author makes one mistake. A comma. A smell. A favorite pen.
I will find it. And then I will make them sign the Loyalty Oath. Twice.

scenes.recap: Dwight and Angela begin the investigation; Angela is unusually eager to suggest Toby.

beats.text: Secretary. Suspects.
Toby. It's obviously Toby. He's sad and he types.
Toby's HR. HR isn't allowed to take the survey.
Then it's Oscar.
I gave him a three out of five. I was generous.

scenes.recap: Michael accuses Toby; Toby wasn't allowed to take the survey, and Kelly volunteers her own glowing comment.

beats.text: Toby. You wrote it. 'Stuck in a room.' That's an HR phrase.
I'm not allowed to take the survey, Michael. Because I'm HR.
That's exactly what someone who took the survey would say.
Michael, I wrote 'Michael is so fun!!!' With three exclamation points. And a heart.
Thank you, Kelly. You are a good daughter.

scenes.recap: Pam tells Roy about the art class; he shrugs that she already draws for free. Darryl tells her to sign up.

beats.text: So there's this art class on Tuesdays. Eighty dollars. I was thinking about it.
You already draw, though. Why pay to do something you already do?
To get better at it?
Tuesdays is darts, babe. I'll be out anyway. Do whatever.
Sign up, Pam. Life's short. I took a keyboard class. Best eighty dollars I ever spent.

scenes.recap: Dwight finds a misspelling in the comment that matches Angela's party memos; he realizes she wrote it, and closes the folder.

beats.caption: holds the comment next to a Party Planning Committee memo

beats.text: 'Together.' Spelled with two Gs. 'Togethger.' The same as on the birthday memo.
That's a common mistake.
It is a common mistake.

beats.caption: closes the folder and puts it in the shredder pile

lines: I don't regret it. Michael made us do a trust fall in August. I fell. Nobody caught me.
But I don't want him sad either. I'm not a monster. I'm a realist.

scenes.recap: Alone, Michael reads the rest of the anonymous comments, which are not all bad.

beats.caption: reads the full stack of comments, one at a time

beats.text: 'Michael remembered my mom's surgery.' 'Michael is annoying, but he's the reason I still work here.'
'Good at birthdays.' That's Kevin. 'Please fewer meetings.' That's everyone.

lines: Sixth out of six. But 'he's the reason I still work here.' Josh from Stamford didn't get that.
Okay, he probably did. But I got it too.

scenes.recap: Dwight reports that the author is unknowable, protecting Angela; Michael lets it go.

beats.text: Michael. The author cannot be found. They are like the wind. Or a ninja. Or a ghost ninja.
That's okay, Dwight. I've decided I don't want to know.
Also, it was probably Stanley. Stanley's going to get the worst birthday this year.

beats.caption: brushes Dwight's sleeve with one finger, on the way out

scenes.recap: Pam signs up for the class; Jim asks to see her sketchbook, and finds a drawing of himself asleep at his desk.

beats.caption: fills out the art class registration form

beats.text: I did it. Tuesdays. Drawing from Life. I'm a student.
Can I see the sketchbook? The famous sketchbook.
Is that... me? Asleep?
You were very still. It's hard to find a still model here.

lines: She drew me. While I was asleep. Which is either really sweet or really creepy.
It's sweet. I'm calling it sweet.

scenes.recap: Michael asks Stanley whether he wrote the comment; Stanley says if he'd written it, it would have been worse.

beats.text: Stanley. Off the record. Did you write the comment?
Michael, if I had written a comment, you would know. It would have been much worse.
That's... weirdly comforting.
